event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: KMB’s 2023-02-09 Form 10-K presents COVID-19 as a still-present, multi-dimensional threat that has already produced measurable operational and financial consequences and could continue to do so.  The company moves beyond generic boiler-plate by documenting concrete, realised impacts since 2020—volatile product demand, supply-chain breakdowns, labour constraints, cost-saving programme delays, remote-work cyber-risk, and ‘unprecedented’ cost inflation in 2021-22.  These disclosures frame COVID-19 both as an historic fact (costs already up, sales already fluctuated) and an ongoing, forward-looking risk whose ultimate magnitude is outside management’s control.  Because the filing date is less than three years after the WHO pandemic declaration, the Time Decay Principle allows relatively high severity scores.  Still, the language is largely qualitative and unquantified, and management cites mitigation efforts, so no single sentence achieves the maximum score.  Overall, the risk evidence is recent, specific and demonstrably material, warranting upper-mid to high micro-scores (3-8 range).

evidence_list.snippet: We face various risks related to health epidemics, pandemics and similar outbreaks, which may have material adverse effects on our business, financial position, results of operations and cash flows.

components.reason: Explicitly identifies pandemics (including COVID-19 by context) as a risk category.
States potential ‘material adverse effects’ across multiple financial dimensions.
Generic, forward-looking statement with no specifics or historic impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct mention of pandemic risk and possible material harm, but statement is broad and unquantified, yielding a moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: The ongoing COVID-19 pandemic has had and could continue to have negative impacts on our business, including causing significant volatility in demand for our products, changes in consumer behavior and preference, disruptions in our manufacturing and supply chain operations, disruptions to our cost saving programs, limitations on our employees’ ability to work and travel, significant changes in the economic or political conditions in markets in which we operate and related currency and commodity volatility.

components.reason: Acknowledges that COVID-19 has already impacted the business (‘has had’).
Lists multiple, specific operational areas affected (demand volatility, supply-chain, labour, cost programmes, FX).
Highlights that impacts may continue into the future.
No monetary quantification.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Recent event, explicit acknowledgement of realised impacts and detailed operational channels drive a high severity score.

evidence_list.snippet: Despite our efforts to manage these impacts, their ultimate impact also depends on factors beyond our knowledge or control, including the duration and severity of any such outbreak and actions taken to contain its spread and mitigate its public health effects.

components.reason: Highlights uncontrollable, uncertain nature of pandemic trajectory.
References management mitigation efforts, signalling partial control.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Sentence underscores uncertainty but is mainly cautionary and partially mitigating, so it receives a low score.

evidence_list.snippet: These activities are subject to inherent risks such as natural disasters, power outages, fires or explosions, labor strikes or labor shortages, terrorism, epidemics, pandemics (including the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic), import restrictions, regional economic, business, environmental or political events (including the war in Ukraine), governmental regulatory requirements or nongovernmental voluntary actions in response to global climate change or other concerns regarding the sustainability of our business, which could disrupt our supply chain and impair our ability to manufacture or sell our products.

components.reason: Explicitly includes ‘pandemics (including the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic)’ among disruptive risks.
Links pandemic risk to concrete outcome: supply-chain disruption and impaired manufacturing/sales.
Long catch-all list dilutes specificity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides a clear linkage to supply-chain disruption but is embedded in a broad list, producing a modest score.

evidence_list.snippet: COVID-19 - The macro business environment experienced unprecedented volatility in recent years related to the continuing effect the global COVID-19 pandemic has had on supply and demand dynamics.

components.reason: Connects COVID-19 directly to ‘unprecedented volatility’ in supply and demand.
Characterises impact as ongoing (‘continuing effect’) and systemic.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Sentence captures recent, systemic market volatility due to COVID-19, justifying a mid-high score.

evidence_list.snippet: In recent years, our sales have fluctuated, especially in Consumer Tissue and K-C Professional, because of COVID-19-related demand spikes, inventory destocking, and consumer usage pattern disruption.

components.reason: Cites actual sales volatility in specific segments tied to COVID-19.
Details underlying mechanisms (demand spikes, destocking, usage changes).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific business segments and realised sales swings raise the severity to the upper-moderate level.

evidence_list.snippet: Additionally, consumer incomes have generally been impacted negatively by the pandemic which can impact their purchasing patterns.

components.reason: Links pandemic to reduced consumer income and demand risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Identifies a demand-side risk but with no quantification or operational detail, resulting in a moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: The pandemic has significantly disrupted supply chains across the globe.

components.reason: Asserts global supply-chain disruption as a realised fact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Concise, high-level statement of realised disruption earns a solid but not top score.

evidence_list.snippet: These effects have caused challenges getting input materials into our production facilities, production delays, and delays and meaningfully higher costs to get products from our production facilities to our customers.

components.reason: Describes concrete operational problems (input shortages, production delays).
Mentions ‘meaningfully higher costs’ already incurred.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Sentence specifies operational and cost impacts already felt, warranting a mid-high score.

evidence_list.snippet: The net effect of the global supply chain disruption led to an unprecedented increase in costs in 2022 and 2021.

components.reason: Attributes cost increases in specific years (2022 and 2021) to pandemic-driven supply chain disruption.
Uses strong language (‘unprecedented’) to indicate magnitude.
No numeric quantification of cost increase.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides a temporal link to actual cost escalation but lacks figures, yielding a solid mid-high score.
